chunks: # Installing Buildkite agent on macOS
The Buildkite agent is supported on macOS 11 (Big Sur) or newer using Homebrew or the Buildkite installer script, and supports pre-release versions of both macOS and Xcode.
## [Installation](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/self-hosted/install/macos\#installation)

We recommend installing the agent using [Homebrew](http://brew.sh/) so you can use the [Buildkite formula repository](https://github.com/buildkite/homebrew-buildkite). If you don't use Homebrew you should follow the [Linux](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/self-hosted/install/linux) install instructions.

## [Which user the agent runs as](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/self-hosted/install/macos\#which-user-the-agent-runs-as)
On macOS, the Buildkite agent runs as the user who started the `launchd` service.

If you need the same configuration on each agent, either configure the `launchd` service to use the [`--spawn` flag](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/cli/reference/start#starting-an-agent-options) on the `buildkite-agent`, or the [`spawn` setting](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/self-hosted/configure#spawn) in the `buildkite-agent.cfg` file.

## [Upgrading](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/self-hosted/install/macos\#upgrading)

If you installed the buildkite-agent using the [Linux install script](https://buildkite.com/docs/agent/self-hosted/install/linux) then you should run the installer script again and it will update your agent.
